issues.legal_issue: A plaintiff seeking specific performance must prove continuous readiness and willingness, including the capacity to pay the balance of the sale consideration.
material_facts: The parties agreed to sell a shop, with part of the price paid as earnest money and the balance due when the sale deed was to be executed.
Although both parties attended the Sub-Registrar’s office on the agreed date, no sale deed was executed.
The plaintiff sued for specific performance but produced no documentary evidence that he had the balance amount available at the relevant time.
The plaintiff said that he had borrowed the money from friends but could not name them or establish that he had raised the money.
The trial court dismissed the suit for failure to prove readiness and willingness; the appellate court and High Court reversed that decision and granted specific performance.
issues.conclusion: The plaintiff failed to prove readiness and willingness because he did not establish his capacity to pay the balance consideration. The appellate court and High Court had not properly assessed the evidence and were wrong to reverse the trial court; the decree for specific performance was set aside.
issues.legal_principle: A plaintiff seeking specific performance must establish readiness and willingness throughout, and must show the capacity to perform the contractual obligation to pay the balance consideration. The relief is discretionary, and the court should examine the plaintiff’s capacity to pay. The judgment cites no statutory provision or earlier case for these principles.

predicates.specific_performance_suit: The proceeding is a suit seeking specific performance of an agreement for sale.
predicates.plaintiff_did_not_prove_capacity_to_pay_: The plaintiff failed to establish that they could pay the balance consideration when required to perform the agreement.
predicates.plaintiff_provided_no_reliable_evidence_: The plaintiff produced no reliable evidence, such as financial records or a negotiable instrument, showing that the required funds were available.
predicates.plaintiff_could_not_substantiate_claimed: The plaintiff claimed to have borrowed the required funds but could not identify the lenders or otherwise establish that the funds had been raised.

issues.definition: When a plaintiff seeks specific performance but fails to prove capacity to pay the balance through reliable evidence or substantiated borrowing, specific performance is denied.

issues.legal_issue: When specific performance is refused after the plaintiff has paid earnest money and deposited the balance consideration, those sums are to be returned with applicable interest.
material_facts: The plaintiff had paid earnest money under the agreement for sale.
After the first appellate court granted specific performance, the plaintiff deposited the balance consideration with that court.
The Supreme Court set aside the decree for specific performance.
The Court directed the sellers to repay the earnest money with interest and permitted the plaintiff to withdraw the deposited balance with any interest accrued on it.
issues.conclusion: The sellers were ordered to repay the earnest money with interest at 12% per annum from the agreement date to the judgment date and thereafter at 10% per annum until payment. The plaintiff was permitted to withdraw the deposited balance consideration with any interest accrued on it.
issues.legal_principle: After setting aside the decree for specific performance, the Court directed repayment of the earnest money with interest and allowed withdrawal of the balance consideration deposited in the appellate court. The judgment cites no statutory provision or earlier case for this direction.

predicates.specific_performance_claim_rejected: The court refused the plaintiff’s claim for specific performance.
predicates.plaintiff_paid_earnest_money: The plaintiff paid earnest money to the other party under the agreement.
predicates.plaintiff_deposited_balance_consideratio: The plaintiff deposited the balance consideration with a court during the proceedings.

issues.definition: If a specific-performance claim is rejected after the plaintiff paid earnest money and deposited the balance consideration, the payments are returned with applicable interest.
